name: Plants
tagline: The green engine of the biosphere
description: From towering redwoods to floating duckweed, plants convert sunlight into the energy that powers nearly every food web on Earth. This section covers trees, shrubs, herbs, aquatic plants, carnivorous oddities and more.

name: Flowers
description: Flowers are the reproductive marvels of angiosperms — evolved billboards designed to attract bees, birds, bats and beetles. Explore roses, lotuses, orchids, night bloomers and national flowers.

name: Insects
description: Insects make up more than half of all described species. Pollinators, decomposers, engineers and pests — they hold ecosystems together.

name: Butterflies & Moths
description: 180,000+ species of butterflies and moths, famous for metamorphosis, migration and the most dazzling wing patterns in the animal kingdom.

name: Mammals
description: Big cats, whales, bats, primates and pangolins — mammals occupy every habitat from Himalayan snowfields to the deep ocean.

name: Reptiles
description: Snakes, lizards, crocodilians, turtles and the lone tuatara — ectotherms that rule deserts, rivers and rainforests.

name: Amphibians
description: Frogs, toads, salamanders, newts and caecilians. Their permeable skin makes them the planet's most sensitive environmental indicators.

name: Fishes
tagline: From mountain streams to the midnight zone
description: 35,000+ species of fish — sharks and rays, reef jewels, river giants and bizarre bioluminescent hunters of the deep sea.

name: Birds
description: Eagles, owls, hummingbirds, penguins and peacocks — 10,000+ species that colonised every continent and the open ocean.

name: Marine Life
tagline: Invertebrate wonders of the blue planet
description: Octopuses, jellyfish, corals, crabs and plankton — the invertebrates that build reefs and feed the oceans.

name: Arachnids
description: Spiders, scorpions, ticks and mites — ancient predators with silk, venom and sensory superpowers.

name: Worms
description: Earthworms, leeches, silkworms and marine bristle worms — humble animals with outsized ecological and economic impact.

name: Microorganisms
description: Bacteria, archaea, protozoa, algae and viruses. Microbes invented photosynthesis, fixed our nitrogen and live inside every one of us.

name: Fungi
description: Mushrooms, moulds, yeasts, lichens and truffles — a kingdom closer to animals than plants, linking forests through underground networks.

name: Extinct Species
tagline: Life that no longer walks with us
description: Dinosaurs, mammoths, the dodo and the thylacine. More than 99% of all species that ever lived are now extinct — these are their stories.
